key_insight: In 2D stochastic vortex dynamics, SALT preserves circulation but amplifies high-frequency sensitivity, while SFLT preserves energy and spreads uncertainty more diffusely across the flow.
engineering_relevance: The choice between SALT and SFLT determines whether uncertainty modeling is localized around sharp vortical features or regularized across the full domain, which matters for turbulence simulation and reduced-order design.
method: Compare two geometric stochastic Euler formulations: SALT and SFLT
Analyze how noise couples to flow scales, especially high-wavenumber modes
Test both methods on traveling dipole, vortex merger, and forced-damped turbulence
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing SALT uncertainty concentrated near active vorticity gradients, whereas SFLT produces a broader variance field across the domain.
watch_item: Preserving both circulation and energy is not generally possible except via a stochastic time reparametrization, so the modeling choice must be made deliberately.
paper_title: Numerical comparison of energy- versus circulation-preserving stochastic vortex dynamics
